_comment: Forming-tool library (cad-fork G07 slice 4a). Each tool is a punch solid standing on the sheet face: its top face lies in the sheet face, the body goes into the sheet. 'depth' is how far the punch goes below the sheet face and must be at least the sheet thickness T for the formed wall to be T thick. Proportions are rule-of-thumb defaults from public fabrication design guides (see each source); they are starting points and must be checked against the fabricator's tooling. Lengths in mm, angles in degrees.

tools.name: dimple
tools.description: Conical dimple (pressed-in cone frustum, closed bottom), for stiffening or locating a fastener head.

top_diameter.doc: Diameter of the dimple at the sheet face

bottom_diameter.doc: Diameter of the dimple floor (smaller than the top)

depth.doc: Depth of the punch below the sheet face (at least T)

tools.source: Fabricator DFM guides for dimples (for example fabcon.com sheet-metal DFM guide: keep a cut-out edge at least 4T plus the dimple inner radius away from a dimple); cone-frustum geometry and 1T wall are the design choices here.

tools.name: extruded_hole
tools.description: Extruded (flanged) through hole: a round hole with a collar of the sheet's own thickness drawn out below the sheet.

hole_diameter.doc: Inside diameter of the collar (the hole)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face; the collar sticks out depth minus T below the sheet

tools.source: Extruded-hole (collar) practice in sheet-metal design guides: collar wall about T, hole diameter at least about 2T; geometry here is the cylinder punch with an open end.

tools.name: countersunk_hole
tools.description: Countersunk through hole formed by a 90 degree cone punch with a short cylindrical stub.

countersink_diameter.doc: Diameter of the countersink at the sheet face

angle.doc: Included angle of the countersink cone (ISO and ASME flat-head screws use 90 degrees; some inch screws use 82)

stub.doc: Length of the cylindrical stub below the cone

tools.source: ISO 10642 / ASME B18.6.3 flat countersunk head screws (90 degree head); countersink diameter and wall conventions from fabricator guides.

tools.name: rib
tools.description: Embossed stiffening rib (bead): a slot-shaped pressed-in channel with closed ends.

width.doc: Rib width at the sheet face

length.doc: Overall rib length (at least the width)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face (at least T)

tools.source: Stiffening-rib (bead) practice in sheet-metal design guides: depth about 2T to 3T, width several times T; slot-shaped plan with vertical walls is the simplification used here.

tools.name: louver
tools.description: Louver: a sloped, trapezoid-section flap lanced free at both ends and pushed below the sheet to let air through.

width.doc: Louver extent along the sheared ends (y)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face (at least T)

slope_inset.doc: Horizontal run of each sloped side

tools.source: Louver practice in sheet-metal design guides: a louver is a partly sheared, formed slit whose height is limited to a few T; the open (sheared) ends are modelled as open faces of the punch.

tools.name: lance
tools.description: Lance (tab): a flap sheared on three sides and bent below the sheet along a ramp.

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face at the high end (at least T)

tools.source: Lance/tab forming in sheet-metal design guides (partial shear and bend; height limited to a few T); modelled as a single sloped face with the three sheared sides open.
